$description: UberTib PRIMITIVE typography. Literal type values live only in this file. Arabic-first: the scale, the leading and the tracking rule are set by Arabic rendering, and Latin follows. A component never references a primitive; it goes through the semantic layer.

ui.$description: The single UI family for all three platforms. The Arabic face leads so Arabic renders from it; the Latin companion catches Latin glyphs inside Arabic text with related design and vertical metrics. No second display or editorial family exists.

mono.$description: Machine identifiers only - correlation and idempotency keys, content hashes, raw audit payload keys - on Admin and audit surfaces. Never body copy, never a label, never a price, never a date, and never present on a Patient surface.

fontSize.$description: Explicit scale, not a pure ratio. Values below 14px are Latin-metadata-only: Arabic at 12px loses its diacritics on a phone screen.

100.$description: Latin metadata only. Prohibited for Arabic and for any essential text.

200.$description: Dense Latin numerals and codes inside operational tables.

300.$description: Floor for Arabic text anywhere. Panel dense text.

fontWeight.$description: Four weights. Weight carries hierarchy; weight never carries a lifecycle state, because Arabic weight differentiation is weaker than Latin and is unreliable as a sole signal.

lineHeight.$description: Unitless multipliers, set for Arabic. Every value is looser than the Latin equivalent because Arabic ascenders, descenders and diacritics collide at Latin leading. The 1.25 heading leading a Latin scale would use is deliberately absent.

tight.$description: Headings only. The tightest leading Arabic diacritics survive.

snug.$description: Dense operational rows and single-line labels.

relaxed.$description: Long Patient reading passages and largest supported text size.

letterSpacing.$description: One value, deliberately. Non-zero letter spacing breaks Arabic glyph joining and turns a word into disconnected letterforms, so no tracking scale is defined for any surface.

measure.$description: Line length ceilings in characters, for the Patient reading column.
